SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--First parenthetical note in the "Pre-season shopping in October continues to accelerate" section of release dated Sept. 28, 2026 should read "which became an annual tradition in 2022" (instead of "which began in 2021").

The updated release reads:

ADOBE: U.S. HOLIDAY SHOPPING SEASON TO HIT RECORD $275.1 BILLION ONLINE, RISING 6.7% YOY

  • Cyber Monday set to remain the biggest online shopping day of the season—with consumers spending over $15 billion in a single day—but Black Friday will see stronger growth due to earlier discounts.
  • Consumers are expected to take advantage of competitive deals this season (up to 30% off listed price) to stock up on essentials such as personal hygiene and household cleaning products.
  • The overall shopping journey continues to evolve, as consumers embrace AI tools and social influencers to find deals and learn about specific products, while continuing to leverage Buy Now Pay Later when they are ready to transact.

Adobe (Nasdaq: ADBE) released today its online shopping forecast for the 2026 holiday season, covering the period from Nov. 1 to Dec. 31, 2026. Based on Adobe Analytics data, the analysis provides the most comprehensive view into U.S. e-commerce by analyzing direct transactions online. Adobe’s forecast is based on over 1 trillion visits to U.S. retail sites, 100 million SKUs and 18 product categories—more than any other technology company or research organization. Adobe Analytics is part of Adobe CX Enterprise, relied upon by global brands to accelerate Customer Experience Orchestration, connecting data, content and AI to deliver real-time, personalized interactions.

2026 holidays set to cross $275 billion milestone, with pre-season spending uptick in October

Adobe expects U.S. online sales to hit $275.1 billion this holiday season (Nov. 1 to Dec. 31, 2026), growing 6.7% year-over-year (YoY). Cyber Week (the five-day period between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday) is set to drive $47.5 billion online (up 7.4% YoY), representing 17.3% of the full holiday season spend.

Cyber Monday (Nov. 30) is expected to set a new milestone for U.S. e-commerce, with consumers spending over $15 billion online in a single day ($15.1 billion, up 6.2% YoY). The second biggest day of the season will be Black Friday ($12.9 billion, up 9.2% YoY), which is growing faster than Cyber Monday—driven in part by having the biggest discounts for categories such as TVs, apparel and appliances. Thanksgiving is set to drive $6.9 billion (up 8.5% YoY), bolstered by impulse shopping: A record 63% of online spend is set to come through mobile devices (up from 61.6% in 2025), outpacing the full season where mobile will account for 57.4% of overall spend (up from 56.4% in 2025).

Of the full holiday season spend, electronics ($63.3 billion, up 5.9% YoY) and apparel ($51.3 billion, up 4.7% YoY) remain tentpole categories in e-commerce, but consumers are also embracing other categories online with stronger growth observed in furniture ($33.4 billion, up 7.3% YoY), grocery ($26.1 billion, up 10.3% YoY), toys ($9.6 billion, up 9.6% YoY) and cosmetics ($9.2 billion, 9.5% YoY).

Pre-season shopping in October continues to accelerate

The Prime Day event in October (which became an annual tradition in 2022) has become an industrywide e-commerce moment, with discounts happening broadly across U.S. retailers. It is now driving significant consumer spend in advance of the holiday season. Adobe expects $95.8 billion will be spent online in October 2026, up a notable 8% YoY. Nearly $10 billion will be spent during the Prime Day event from October 6 to 7 ($9.9 billion, up 9.2% YoY), driven in part by discounts that are set to peak at 19% off listed price. This has changed the shape of the holiday season, pushing U.S. retailers to manage promotions and inventory effectively to capture an additional pre-season spike in shopping interest.

Consumers expected to take advantage of strong discounts to stock up on essentials

Adobe expects competitive discounts this holiday season, up to 30% off listed price (during Cyber Week). Shoppers will see deals throughout the season, up to 14% in early November, up to 21% just before Thanksgiving and up to 10-15% throughout December.

Across categories, deals will be on par with the 2025 season: Discounts in electronics for example, are expected to peak at 30% off listed price (vs. 30.1% in 2025), while discounts for toys are set to hit 29% (vs. 28%). Notable discounts are also expected in TVs at 23% (vs. 24.2%), computers at 23% (vs. 22.8%), apparel at 23% (vs. 23.2%), sporting goods at 19% (vs. 19.5%), appliances at 18% (vs. 19.2%) and furniture at 18% (vs. 19%). Shoppers will find the deepest discounts for electronics and computers on Cyber Monday, but the best deals for TVs, toys, apparel, appliances and furniture is expected to land on Black Friday. Thanksgiving will have the best deals for sporting goods.

While consumers have historically embraced holiday deals to buy gifts or adopt the latest gadgets, many are taking advantage of discounts to stock up on essentials. During Cyber Week, online sales of personal hygiene products are expected to jump 150% (compared to average sales levels in September 2026) and clothing basics by 210%. Other essentials set to see a boost include baby products (up 113%), pet products (up 93%) and household cleaning items (up 49%).

Buy Now Pay Later to drive over $21 billion in holiday season spend

The flexible payment method continues to see traction amongst consumers during the holiday season. Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) is expected to drive $21.3 billion (Nov-Dec), up 6.6% YoY. Usage is set to spike on Cyber Monday, where BNPL will be used for $1.09 billion in online spend. This is the second consecutive year where over a billion dollars were driven by BNPL on Cyber Monday. On Black Friday, BNPL is set to drive $807 million in online spend. Most of BNPL spend will come through mobile devices (82% share vs. desktop), showing the impact of impulse shopping on driving adoption of the payment method.

Additional Adobe Analytics insights

  • Another AI-powered holiday season: In the 2024 holiday season, Adobe observed the first uptick in consumers using AI-powered chat and browser services for online shopping (from finding deals to quickly locating products). Adobe expects AI traffic to U.S. retail sites this holiday season (measured by shoppers clicking on a link) to rise 130% YoY. The biggest uptick is expected on Thanksgiving (up 159% YoY), followed by Black Friday (up 95% YoY) and Cyber Monday (up 88% YoY). In an Adobe survey* of 5,000 consumers, 77% of respondents who have used AI for online shopping report feeling more confident in their purchase, and 69% say they are less likely to return an item they bought.
  • Hot sellers: Top gaming consoles this season are expected to include Nintendo Switch 2, Sony PlayStation 5/Pro and Xbox Series X, along with games such as Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, EA SPORTS FC 27, Grand Theft Auto VI, Madden NFL 27, Marvel’s Wolverine, Minecraft Dungeons II, NBA 2K27 and Pokémon Pokopia. Top selling toys are expected to include Beyblade X, Jellycat plush toys, KPop Demon Hunters toys, LEGO Pokémon and SMART Play, NeeDoh Toys, Pokémon Pikachu Puppetronic, Sesame Street Tickle Me Elmo Giggle Max and Toy Story 5 toys. Other expected hot sellers include AirPods Pro 3​, Dyson Airwrap​, Google Pixel 11​, iPhone 18 Pro​, iPhone Duo, KODAK Charmera​, Meta AI Glasses, Oura Ring 5​, Samsung Galaxy S26/Z Fold8​ and WHOOP 5.0.
  • Social media and affiliates drive purchase behavior: Adobe measures the impact of different marketing investments during the holiday season, looking at its contribution to revenue. Affiliates/partners (which includes social influencers) and social media overall are set to see the biggest gains in share of revenue, up 12% and 17%, respectively. In comparison, paid search is expected to rise by 4%. Within the affiliates/partner category, cashback and rewards partners leads in affiliate traffic with a 36% share, followed by influencers and creators at 22%. For U.S. retailers, this highlights the importance of partner and social-led acquisition during the holiday season.

Key Terms

skutechnical
A SKU (stock keeping unit) is a unique code a company assigns to a specific product variant—think of it as a product’s name tag that distinguishes size, color, model or packaging. Investors use SKUs to track which items sell, how fast inventory turns, and where profit comes from, so they reveal customer demand, supply-chain efficiency and revenue drivers much like each item in a supermarket tells the store which shelves are performing.
buy now pay laterfinancial
Buy now, pay later is a short-term consumer financing option that lets shoppers split a purchase into scheduled payments instead of paying the full amount up front; lenders or payment providers pay the merchant immediately and collect the installments from the buyer. Investors care because this model can boost sales and merchant fees but also creates credit risk, regulatory exposure, and sensitivity to consumer spending trends—like giving a store a small loan to help sales grow.

CULVER CITY, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--ImmunityBio, Inc. (NASDAQ: IBRX), a commercial-stage immunotherapy company, today announced the publication of long-term data from the Phase 2/3 QUILT-3.032 study (N=100) in the Journal of Urology. The study evaluated ANKTIVA® (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln) in combination with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) in patients with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS), with or without papillary disease.

Highlights:

  • 71% complete response (CR) rate in patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC CIS, with or without papillary disease
  • Median duration of CR of 26.6 months, with responses extending beyond 53 months
  • More than half of responding patients in the FDA-reviewed population maintained complete responses beyond 45 months
  • 84% cystectomy-free survival at 36 months among responders
  • 98.2% disease-specific survival at three years
  • No Grade 4 or Grade 5 treatment-related adverse events reported

“The QUILT-3.032 study represents one of the longest follow-up data sets in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC to date, and the results continue to support the durability of ANKTIVA’s unique mechanism of action in generating sustained immune responses,” said Patrick Soon-Shiong, M.D., Founder, Executive Chairman and Global Chief Scientific and Medical Officer of ImmunityBio. “These long-term findings are encouraging, suggesting the potential for prolonged disease control and the possibility of avoiding or delaying radical cystectomy for some patients.”

The publication also reported:

  • 63.8% of responders maintained CR for at least 12 months
  • 52.3% maintained CR for at least 24 months
  • 44.2% maintained CR for at least 36 months
  • Progression-free survival remained 80.9% at three years
  • In BCG refractory (never responded) patients, the CR rate was 66%
  • 4% of responders progressed to muscle-invasive disease

The treatment continued to demonstrate a favorable safety profile. Most treatment-related adverse events were Grade 1 or Grade 2 and consisted of localized bladder symptoms associated with intravesical therapy. Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 4% of patients, with no Grade 4 or Grade 5 treatment-related adverse events reported.

“Achieving a durable response and avoiding cystectomy are important treatment goals for patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC,” said Richard Adcock, President and CEO of ImmunityBio. “These peer-reviewed results add to the growing body of evidence supporting ANKTIVA plus BCG and highlight its potential to provide sustained disease control and meaningful cystectomy avoidance for patients with limited treatment options. We thank the patients and clinical teams who contributed to this long-term follow-up.”

The publication builds upon the growing body of clinical evidence supporting ANKTIVA plus BCG, which was initially approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2024 for the treatment of adult patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with CIS, with or without papillary tumors. In October 2026, the FDA expanded the approved indication to include patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with papillary-only disease. ANKTIVA is the first FDA-approved IL-15 receptor agonist and the first approved immunotherapy in NMIBC designed to activate natural killer (NK) cells and T cells to generate durable immune responses.

About the QUILT 3.032 Study

QUILT-3.032 (NCT03022825) is a multicenter Phase 2/3 study evaluating ANKTIVA plus BCG in patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC. The published analysis includes 100 patients with CIS with or without papillary disease and represents one of the longest follow-up datasets reported in this disease setting, with outcomes extending beyond five years in some patients.

About ANKTIVA® (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln)

The interleukin-15 (IL-15) cytokine plays a crucial role in the immune system by affecting the development, maintenance, and function of key immune cells—NK and CD8+ killer T cells—that are involved in killing cancer cells. By activating NK cells, ANKTIVA® overcomes the tumor escape phase of clones resistant to T cells and restores memory T cell activity with resultant prolonged duration of complete response. ANKTIVA® is a first-in-class IL-15 receptor agonist IgG1 fusion complex, consisting of an IL-15 mutant (IL-15N72D) fused with an IL-15 receptor alpha, which binds with high affinity to IL-15 receptors on NK, CD4+, and CD8+ T cells. This fusion complex of ANKTIVA® mimics the natural biological properties of the membrane-bound IL-15 receptor alpha, delivering IL-15 by dendritic cells and driving the activation and proliferation of NK cells with the generation of memory killer T cells that have retained immune memory against these tumor clones.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

INDICATION AND USAGE: ANKTIVA® is an interleukin-15 (IL-15) receptor agonist indicated with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) for the treatment of adult patients with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS) with or without papillary tumors.

WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS: Risk of Metastatic Bladder Cancer with Delayed Cystectomy. Delaying cystectomy can lead to the development of muscle-invasive or metastatic bladder cancer, which can be lethal. If patients with CIS do not have a complete response to treatment after a second induction course of ANKTIVA® with BCG, reconsider cystectomy.

DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION: For Intravesical Use Only. Do not administer by subcutaneous or intravenous routes.

Please see the complete Indication and Important Safety Information and Prescribing Information for ANKTIVA® at Anktiva.com.

ImmunityBio, Inc. is a biotechnology company focused on innovating, developing, and commercializing next-generation immunotherapies designed to activate the patient’s immune system and deliver durable protection against cancer and infectious diseases. Our approach harnesses both the adaptive and innate immune systems with the goal of restoring immune function and generating lasting immunological memory in patients. Key Terms

nmibcmedical
A common form of bladder cancer that stays confined to the bladder’s inner lining or the layer just below it and has not grown into the deeper muscle wall. It matters to investors because it often requires repeated procedures, ongoing surveillance and long-term treatments, creating a sizable and stable market for diagnostics, drugs and medical devices; think of it like a surface-level problem that needs frequent check-ups and follow-up care rather than a one-time fix.
cismedical
Cis is a descriptor from chemistry meaning two parts of a molecule sit on the same side of a bond or ring, like two passengers sitting on the same side of a seesaw. That arrangement can change a drug’s shape, how it behaves in the body, and whether regulators approve it or competitors can patent it. Investors watch “cis” versus “trans” forms because those small structural differences can affect safety, effectiveness, manufacturing and commercial value.
intravesicalmedical
Intravesical describes a medical treatment or procedure where a drug or therapy is placed directly into the bladder through a catheter rather than taken by mouth or injected into the bloodstream. For investors, it signals a focused delivery method that can increase local effectiveness and reduce whole‑body side effects, often affecting a product’s clinical value, patient convenience, regulatory path, and market niche — like watering a plant at its roots instead of spraying its leaves.
progression-free survivalmedical
Progression-free survival is the length of time during and after a treatment that a patient's disease does not get worse, measured from the start of treatment until the disease shows measurable signs of progression or the patient dies. Investors care because longer progression-free survival in clinical trials often signals that a drug is effective, improving chances of regulatory approval, market adoption, and revenue potential—think of it as a stopwatch showing how long a therapy can keep the illness at bay.
il-15 receptor agonistmedical
An IL-15 receptor agonist is a drug or biologic that turns on the same cell-surface switch used by the immune-signaling protein interleukin-15, boosting the activity and number of immune cells that seek and destroy infected or abnormal cells. For investors, these agents matter because they can improve the effectiveness of cancer and infectious disease treatments but also carry safety and regulatory risks that strongly affect clinical trial outcomes and commercial prospects.

TEMECULA, CA / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / Hop-on, Inc. (OTCID:HPNN) today announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, Digitalage, Inc., has developed a working pilot console for its AI-assisted news-video infrastructure, demonstrating an end-to-end workflow that moves source material through editorial review, video production, quality control, cataloging and delivery.

The pilot advances Digitalage beyond individual media-generation tools toward a broader operating layer designed for publishers, news organizations, communications companies and enterprises that need to produce media at scale while preserving source traceability, editorial control and an operating record.

Digitalage is building around the full media lifecycle:

INGEST. VERIFY. PRODUCE. REVIEW. GOVERN. DELIVER.

Peter Michaels, Chairman and CEO of Hop-on, Inc. and Founder and Chairman of Digitalage, said:

"This is exactly what I mean when I say Digitalage is infrastructure, not another AI video generator."

"Generating a video is the easy part. The bigger problem is everything around it. Where did the story come from? What source supports it? Who approved it? Did it pass quality review? Can it be changed without rebuilding everything? Where was it delivered? Can you prove what happened?"

"Anyone can push a button and make a video. We are building the infrastructure behind the button."

THREE PATHS FROM SOURCE TO VIDEO

The current pilot demonstrates three distinct production workflows.

The first allows an authorized user to provide source text and produce a video using an AI presenter.

The second allows incoming feed content to trigger production automatically through configurable rules, allowing those rules to determine whether material proceeds through the workflow without manual intervention.

The third provides an editorially controlled path in which a proposed script is checked against its underlying source material and held for human approval before rendering begins.

Together, those workflows are intended to allow organizations to automate routine production without surrendering editorial authority when human review is required.

AN OPERATING SYSTEM AROUND THE MEDIA

The working pilot brings multiple production, editorial and governance functions into a unified console.

Capabilities demonstrated by the Digitalage development team include:

  • Source-text and feed-based story ingestion
  • AI-presenter video generation
  • Rule-based automated processing
  • Source-to-script editorial review
  • Human approval before rendering
  • A 14-stage rendering workflow
  • A 71-check video quality report
  • Story and editorial management
  • Feed and automation-rule management
  • Media cataloging
  • Reusable brand kits
  • Signed webhook delivery
  • Per-run API capability validation and usage tracking

The system currently includes 87 working API capabilities.

The console tracks which capabilities are exercised and validated during each individual workflow run. Accordingly, a display such as "4 of 87" reflects the number of capabilities used or validated in that specific run, not the number of capabilities available or functioning across the system.

Automated testing, engineering review, improvements and bug fixes continue across the platform.

Digitalage is developing the architecture as a multi-vendor environment rather than one dependent on a single AI model or provider.

The objective is infrastructure capable of orchestrating the tools each workflow requires.

AUTOMATION WITHOUT REMOVING ACCOUNTABILITY

Digitalage believes artificial intelligence will dramatically increase the speed and volume at which media can be created.

The company also believes greater automation makes provenance, source traceability, editorial controls and auditable production processes more important, not less.

The Digitalage architecture is being designed so routine workflows can be automated while organizations retain human approval where editorial policy requires it.

The system is also being developed to preserve underlying source material and production state so changes can be made within the workflow rather than forcing an editor to rebuild an entire production from the beginning.

Robert T. Braun, CEO of Digitalage, said:

"Enterprise customers do not simply need another tool that can generate content. They need reliability, repeatability, governance, control and an operating record."

"As these systems scale, the value is not simply in creating another piece of media. It is in maintaining the source, rights, editorial decisions, production state and delivery history around that media."

"That is what turns a collection of AI tools into enterprise infrastructure."

THE MEDIA KEEPS ITS HISTORY

Most generative tools are designed to produce an output.

Digitalage is being developed around a different model:

The finished media should retain an operating record of how it came into existence.

That record is designed to include the underlying source material, script development, editorial decisions, approval state, production stages, quality review, catalog identity and delivery history.

The objective is to allow an organization to know not only what was published, but also how it got there.

That distinction becomes increasingly important as organizations move from manually producing individual pieces of content to using artificial intelligence and automation to produce media at scale.

Michaels said:

"A finished video should not become a dead file the moment it is rendered."

"We want the source, the decisions, the approvals, the production history and the delivery record to remain connected to the media."

"Most AI tools give you an output. We are building infrastructure that remembers how the output was created."

ONE INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER ACROSS THE MEDIA LIFECYCLE

The news-video console is part of a broader Digitalage architecture being developed across live broadcasting, replay, recorded media, creator monetization, moderation, provenance, searchable catalogs, AI-assisted publishing, rights-aware workflows and enterprise licensing.

Digitalage is also being designed to work alongside production tools creators already use.

Rather than requiring creators to abandon established broadcasting workflows or audiences, Digitalage is designed to accept streams through workflows compatible with production environments such as OBS.

The strategy is straightforward:

CREATORS SHOULD NOT HAVE TO START OVER SIMPLY TO ADD DIGITALAGE.

OBS functions as a production control room where creators can manage cameras, audio and graphics before sending a live stream to an audience.

Digitalage's stream-key workflow is designed to allow creators to add Digitalage alongside existing broadcast channels rather than requiring them to replace those channels.

Digitalage's creator application, currently in testing, connects multiple portions of this lifecycle, including live broadcasting, replay, timed interaction, catalogs and access-pass payment functionality.

When a live event ends, the Digitalage model is designed to continue.

The live stream can become a replay.

The replay can become part of the creator's catalog.

Conversation can remain connected to the moment that created it.

The resulting media can continue creating opportunities for discovery, access and monetization.

The same architectural philosophy now extends into news production.

A story can begin as source material, move through structured editorial and production stages, become finished media and enter a persistent catalog rather than existing only as a one-time AI render.

Digitalage summarizes the model with a simple principle:

"Live is the moment. The catalog is the business."

FROM WORKING PILOT TO COMMERCIAL DEPLOYMENT

With the core workflow now demonstrated, Digitalage's next phase is focused on converting the pilot into deployable enterprise infrastructure.

Current work includes production hardening, performance testing, determining finished-media production costs, configuring customer-specific workflows, establishing pricing and finalizing commercial billing architecture for the newsroom product.

The current news-video pilot operates on a local development stack, and certain production components remain under continuous review, testing and development.

Digitalage is not announcing commercial revenue or a completed customer deployment from the newsroom pilot at this time.

The company intends to demonstrate the system to prospective publishers, news organizations, communications companies and enterprise customers as development reaches the appropriate stage.

Signed commercial agreements and deployments will be announced when and if they are finalized.

The objective is now to move from demonstrated technology to controlled commercial deployment.

DIGITALAGE: NOT A PLATFORM. INFRASTRUCTURE.

Digitalage's development work now spans multiple interconnected layers of the media lifecycle, including live broadcasting, replay, VOD, creator access and monetization, moderation, content processing, searchable media, AI-assisted production and enterprise workflows.

Rather than developing isolated applications for each media format or tying the company's future to a single artificial-intelligence provider, Digitalage is pursuing an infrastructure model in which live, recorded, human-created and AI-assisted media can operate through a shared underlying architecture.

Michaels concluded:

"We spent years building pieces of this architecture. Now those pieces are beginning to work together."

"Live. Replay. Verification. Moderation. News production. Rights. Delivery. Monetization."

"Not a platform. Infrastructure."

Through Digitalage, the company is developing stateful media infrastructure for live and recorded content, creator media, publishing workflows, provenance, content governance, searchable catalogs, rights-aware distribution and monetization.

NORTH EAST, PA / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / NFI Empire, a fully owned subsidiary of Newport Gold, Inc. (OTCID:NWPG), today announced that American Force Wheels has joined Project Reborn-001 as a key partner. The custom vehicle build is heading to auction at The Red Bird Games in Brentwood, TN, with proceeds benefiting The Brett Boyer Foundation. American Force is supplying custom forged N33 Barrage DRW wheels that will be wrapped in 37x13.50R22 tires, giving the one-of-one dually its bold, purpose-driven stance.

Rendering of Project Reborn-001, the 1979 Chevrolet K30 crew cab dually, rolling on American Force forged wheels.

The Build Update

Project Reborn-001 continues its transformation of a 1979 Chevrolet K30 crew cab into a modern performance powerhouse, pairing the classic square-body exterior with a contemporary GMC Sierra 3500 frame, Duramax diesel drivetrain, suspension, and amenities. American Force Wheels has contributed its N33 Barrage wheels in 22-inch DRW (dual rear wheel) configuration. The N33 Barrage is part of American Force's forged monoblock aluminum lineup, engineered for strength and reduced weight while delivering the aggressive styling expected of a high-end custom dually. These wheels will be wrapped with 37x13.50R22 tires, completing the truck's unmistakable ground-pounding presence as it prepares for SEMA and its live auction benefiting The Brett Boyer Foundation. Consistent progress updates will continue to be shared as the build advances.

American Force N33 Barrage forged wheel mounted with a 37x13.50R22 tire.

The N33 Barrage forged monoblock aluminum wheel in a polished finish.

"Project REBORN represents what the automotive community can accomplish when great companies come together behind an even greater purpose," said Jason Sandusky of American Force Wheels. "We're proud to support NFI Empire and The Brett Boyer Foundation and to put American Force wheels on a build that will ultimately help children and families affected by congenital heart disease. REBORN-001 is going to be an incredible truck, but knowing what it represents and the impact it can make is what makes being part of this project truly special."- Jason Sandusky, Marketing / Event / Partnership Management, American Force

"Partnering with American Force Wheels on Project Reborn-001 brings American-made forged strength and style that perfectly complement the performance and purpose of this extraordinary build," said Justin Fried, CEO of Newport Gold, Inc. and NFI Empire. "Every component on this truck exists to amplify awareness and funding for The Brett Boyer Foundation's work against congenital heart disease and in celebration of the Down syndrome community."

What is The Brett Boyer Foundation

The Brett Boyer Foundation is a Nashville, Tennessee-based nonprofit charitable organization founded in 2017 by Ellen and Bo Boyer in loving memory of their daughter, Sadie Brett Boyer, who was diagnosed prenatally with Down syndrome and a congenital heart defect. Sadie Brett may have only lived for 7 months, but her impact has reached countless children and families, ultimately changing the medical industry by providing kids an edge and fighting chance against CHD. Congenital heart disease (CHD) is one of the most common conditions affecting infants and one that remains severely underfunded compared to other childhood illnesses. The Brett Boyer Foundation is dedicated to raising awareness and funding research aimed at advancing treatment options while providing support to families and providers navigating a CHD diagnosis. Another mission of The Brett Boyer Foundation is to celebrate the love, capability, and dignity of the Down syndrome community. 50% of babies born with Down syndrome fight CHD. Through fundraising efforts and partnerships with like-minded organizations both in the Nashville area and across the United States, the Foundation works to improve outcomes for children living with heart disease so that fewer families endure the loss the Boyers experienced.

The Brett Boyer Foundation: https://www.thebrettboyerfoundation.org/

Specializing in both single rear wheel and dual rear wheel (DRW) applications, American Force is known for monoblock forged construction that delivers exceptional strength, reduced weight, and bold styling. Grosse Pointe, Michigan, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Broad Arrow Auctions and Private Sales, driven by Hagerty (NYSE: HGTY), is at the forefront of the modern Ferrari collector market as it continues to show significant growth in 2026. Analysis from Hagerty shows a surge in demand for modern supercars which now account for 38 percent of the global collector car auction market. Hypercars have seen a similar increase, representing 32 percent of the auction market, with both segments being driven in large part by the demand for highly desirable Ferrari models.

Broad Arrow Auctions has released another highly desirable lineup of Ferrari hypercars and supercars for its upcoming second annual Las Vegas Auction, set for October 31 in partnership with Concours at Wynn Las Vegas.

Latest highlights are led by a 2025 Ferrari Daytona SP3 (Estimate: $16,000,000 - $18,000,000), chassis number 314846, finished in the exquisite Tailor Made shade of Verde Francesca over a two-tone Nero Alcantara and Mustard Aunde Jeans interior. Offered from its original owner, the curator of an exceptional private collection, the SP3 is one of just 600 examples produced and displays just 81 miles at cataloging. The second model in Ferrari’s sought after “Icona” series, the Daytona SP3 is many things—a rolling tribute to one of the marque’s most triumphant afternoons, a showcase of naturally aspirated engineering at its peak, and quite possibly the final chapter in a mid-engine, naturally aspirated lineage that began nearly sixty years ago. The car on offer is equipped with numerous carbon fiber elements, airbrushed fender shield, a suspension lifter, and a full complement of factory accessories.

“The collector car market has quickly recognized the significance of the Daytona SP3 in Ferrari’s history,” says Barney Ruprecht, Vice President of Auctions for Broad Arrow. “In the few short years since the SP3's reveal, values have climbed sharply, reflecting both the model's extreme exclusivity, and a growing understanding that it may represent the final expression Ferrari’s naturally aspirated V12 for the road. This is a particularly special example of the 600 made, with a bespoke specification that’s sure to appeal to today’s most discerning collectors.”

Additional thrilling Ferrari highlights coming to Broad Arrow Las Vegas Auction include:

2014 Ferrari LaFerrari (Estimate: $8,500,000 - $10,000,000)

This is a low-mileage, extensively specified example of the first hybrid hypercar from Maranello, producing a combined 950 horsepower from its 6.3-liter V12 hybrid powerplant. One of approximately 120 examples delivered new to the US, the LaFerrari on offer is finished in iconic Rosso Corsa over Nero leather with Rosso accents, recently serviced, and accompanied by its battery charger, fitted car cover, and tool kit. It is offered with a two-year Certified Pre-Owned warranty, including coverage of its hybrid battery, valid through October 2028.

2003 Ferrari Enzo (Estimate: $6,500,000 - $8,500,000)

One of only 111 delivered new to the US market, this true driver’s example of Ferrari’s singular turn-of-the-century hypercar shows under 18,000 miles at cataloging. It has been refinished by Carrozzeria Zanasi in Maranello to its original Rosso Corsa and features a Pelle Nera interior. Classiche certified and serviced in 2026 by Ferrari Dallas at a cost exceeding $10,000, this is an eminently usable example of the iconic hypercar that carries the legacy of Enzo Ferrari, prepared to be enjoyed the way its namesake intended.

2011 Ferrari 599 SA Aperta (Estimate: $4,100,000 - $4,500,000)

This exceptionally rare supercar is one of only 80 special series SA Aperta models produced in celebration of Pininfarina’s 80th anniversary. Finished in classic Rosso Corsa over Nero leather with Rosso details, it is offered in near-new condition with just 745 miles, $87,000 in optional extras, and an exhilarating zero-to-62 miles per hour time of 3.6 seconds with a top speed of 202 miles per hour.

Additional modern collectible Ferraris on offer include the just-announced 106-mile time capsule 1997 Ferrari F50, a 2015 Ferrari 458 Speciale A offered without reserve, a 2015 Ferrari 458 Speciale, a 2001 Ferrari 550 Barchetta Pininfarina, and more. View the more than 25 Ferraris on offer in the Las Vegas Auction here.

Following the fantastic results for many Ferrari supercars at Broad Arrow recent Zoute Concours Auction, the company continues its momentum in Europe with its second annual Zürich Auction on November 7, the official auction partner of the renowned Auto Zürich show. Exceptional Ferraris are set for the sale at the Dolder Grand hotel, including two of the market’s most desirable models, offered without reserve.

2015 Ferrari LaFerrari (Estimate: CHF 5'500'000 - CHF 7'500'000 | Offered Without Reserve)

Striking in Bianco Fuji over a Bianchi/Neri leather interior, the LaFerrari on offer in Zürich is one of approximately 50 examples specified with the exposed carbon-fiber roof. This delivery-mileage example is offered with the common “sticky buttons” issue remedied and with a new high-voltage battery. The LaFerrari is a well-cared-for example of an essential acquisition—one of the most significant Ferraris ever built.

2017 Ferrari F12tdf (Estimate: CHF 1'300'000 - CHF 1'500'000 | Offered Without Reserve)

The F12tdf was the last Ferrari model to be styled in collaboration with Pininfarina and features a 6.3-litre V12, the most powerful naturally aspirated V12 when it was introduced. This particular car was delivered new to Switzerland finished in distinctive special-order matte Alluminio Opaco over Nero Alcantara with matter carbon fiber and Giallo accents throughout. Offered with just two owners and 13,601 kilometers from new, this is a recently serviced, compelling example of a highly coveted Ferrari.

View the more than 13 Ferraris on offer in Broad Arrow’s Zürich Auction here.

Broad Arrow Private Sales has connected the buyers and sellers of many of the most in-demand Ferrari supercars in recent months, with successful sales throughout its international network. Recent results include two desirable “non-cat, non-adjust” examples of the iconic F40 supercar in both the US and the UK, a 2024 Ferrari Daytona SP3 in a stunning Atelier specification of Extrarange Nero DS Opaco with Gloss Black wheels, and a superbly preserved 2004 Ferrari Enzo with an unbroken chain of Japanese documentation. Learn more about Broad Arrow Private Sales at broadarrowprivatesales.com.

The market for modern Ferrari supercars is looking stronger than ever, and Broad Arrow is proud to be entrusted by both buyers and sellers to secure new homes for these spectacular pieces of motoring history.   Those interested in the sale or purchase of a Ferrari through either Broad Arrow Auctions or Private Sales are invited to contact a Broad Arrow Car Specialist via info@broadarrowauctions.com or by calling +1 313-312-0780 in North America or +44-2045-920-16 in EMEA.

ALEXANDRIA, Va., Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Burke & Herbert Bank & Trust Company (“Burke & Herbert” or “Bank”) calls for teens, ages 13 – 18, to submit entries for the 2026-27 Lights, Camera, Save! video contest. The contest, organized by the American Bankers Association Foundation, is a national competition that encourages teens to use video to communicate the value of wise money management and encourage other teens to engage in positive financial behavior.

“As a community bank, we are proud to support a contest that encourages teens to help their peers build stronger financial habits,” said Bank Chief Executive Officer David Boyle. “For over a decade, we have seen the impact young people can have through this contest in making financial education relatable. We encourage parents and educators to inspire students to participate and join us in preparing the next generation for a strong financial future.”

To participate, students must create a video, 30-seconds or less in length, about using money wisely and submit a link to the video along with a completed entry form to the bank by December 1, 2026. The contest is open to filmmakers of all experience levels.

Burke & Herbert Bank will host a regional round of judging in Delaware, Kentucky, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and West Virginia. The Bank will select a winner from each state to compete on the national level for one of three cash prizes, including $10,000 for first place, $5,000 for second place, and $2,500 for third place. National contestants will face off head-to-head in the first round of national judging on ABA’s Instagram page which will determine which videos advance to the second round of national judging.

Burke & Herbert Bank is rewarding the top regional winners in each of its six state markets with a $500 prize. The Bank also is awarding a $100 gift card to the teacher of each of the first-place regional winners.

Videos will be judged based on their quality, message, content, and the criteria set forth by the contest's official rules. To learn more about the Lights, Camera, Save! Video Contest, visit burkeandherbertbank.com/contest or email save@burkeandherbertbank.com.
